hardwareHubs.note: The city describes its Bayside industrial zone as home to hundreds of manufacturing and tech companies, from hardware startups to large firms.
A January 2026 article describes El Segundo as a rising hardware startup hub built on aerospace roots and advanced 3D printing.

makerspaces.name: Maker Nexus
makerspaces.note: Nonprofit makerspace with a CNC router, CNC plasma cutters, laser cutters, Prusa and resin 3D printers and an electronics lab.

makerspaces.name: Noisebridge
makerspaces.note: Free-to-visit hackerspace at 272 Capp Street with a laser cutter, wood shop, 3D printer and electronics gear.

makerspaces.name: Jacobs Institute for Design Innovation Makerspace
makerspaces.note: UC Berkeley makerspace with 3D printers, laser cutters, CNC routers and mills, a woodshop, a metal shop and an electronics lab.

events.name: Maker Faire Bay Area
events.note: Maker Faire lists Bay Area editions for 2023, 2024 and 2025.

programs.name: Berkeley SkyDeck with the Jacobs Institute
programs.note: Since February 2024 selected SkyDeck hardware startups get Entrepreneur Maker Passes for the Jacobs makerspace and design specialist support.

specialties.name: Aerospace and defense (Los Angeles area)
specialties.note: Aerospace and defense are the main anchors of the Los Angeles hardware scene, per a 2026 article on El Segundo.

specialties.name: Electronics and tech manufacturing (Fremont)
specialties.note: Fremont's Bayside zone hosts hundreds of manufacturing and tech companies.

support.name: California Manufacturing Technology Consulting (CMTC)
support.note: NIST's state page names CMTC as California's MEP center, but NIST's center page for CMTC is marked Former Center and archived, so the current center is unconfirmed.
